algorithm: JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatch over a request dict list: method lookup, tool call with validated args, result/error envelopes.

classes.desc: JSON-RPC 2.0 server sim: tool registry, JSON-RPC dispatch, resources, and error envelopes.
classes.name: MCPServer

complexity: O(1) per request: method dispatch plus one tool call.
data_flow_ascii:
request list -> MCPServer.handle_request -> method dispatch
tools/call -> call_tool(name, args) -> echo | add | word_count
any method -> {jsonrpc 2.0, id, result|error} response dict
description_sentence: An MCP server simulator that exposes echo, add, and word_count tools plus server info through JSON-RPC 2.0 request handling.
failure_note: Unknown methods and tools return proper JSON-RPC error envelopes (-32601/-32602) instead of raising.

label: mcp_server_sim
output_shape: Prints each JSON-RPC request and its response (results for valid calls, error envelopes for bad methods/tools).
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that serves tools over JSON-RPC 2.0 with proper result and error envelopes.

qa.a: Method names dispatch to handlers: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, and resources/list; anything else is a -32601 error.
A dict maps tool names to (function, schema) pairs; call_tool validates args, runs the function, and wraps the result.
resources/list exposes a server-info resource with the name and version.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python implementing JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatch with a tool registry and structured error handling.
run_notes: No extra flags beyond --seed; the request list is rebuilt from the seed each run.
scaling_note: The in-process dispatch suits demos and tests; a real server would add stdio/HTTP transport and concurrency.
storage_note: No persistence: the tool registry is compiled at startup and no request state is kept.
tradeoff_note: Simulating over dicts keeps it dependency-free and testable, but skips real transport framing.
